This is a weekly series posted every Tuesday to discuss the terms anime fans use today.

Today's word is Anime!

Context

Taken from Wikipedia, the Japanese definition of anime is:

Anime, also informally romanized as animé [...] is the abbreviated pronunciation of "animation" in Japanese, where this term references all animation.

Questions

These questions mostly focus on the Western definition of anime, which I have not included on purpose (and also because there isn't really a wholly agreed definition either).

  • Does aesthetic style matter when classifying anime (keep in mind the typical anime style versus something like Panty and Stocking)?
  • Does animation style matter (2D vs 3D) matter when classifying anime?
  • Original air location (keep in mind Space Dandy came out in America first)?
  • Is RWBY an anime?
  • Which definition of 'anime' takes precedence? Western (location of most people on the sub) or Eastern (the country of the term's origin)?

DISCLAIMER: The discussion will have no effect on what is and isn't allowed on the sub

EDIT: Links etc.
[DISCUSSION] Anime Lexicon - Anime | What is anime? (7/14/2015)

Does aesthetic style matter when classifying anime (keep in mind the typical anime style versus something like Panty and Stocking)?

Of course not.

Does animation style matter (2D vs 3D) matter when classifying anime?

No, there always have been 2D anime with 3D rendered characters or mecha. Technology has advanced so that most of them don't seem out of place. Recently there are even anime that is entirely 3D rendered, like Arpeggio of Blue Steel and Expelled from Paradise.

Original air location (keep in mind Space Dandy came out in America first)?

No.

Is RWBY an anime?

Is a MMD web series you see on the Nico Nico Douga an anime? No. Not even those made in Japan.

Which definition of 'anime' takes precedence? Western (location of most people on the sub) or Eastern (the country of the term's origin)?

If we're talking about the term "anime" only, then it literally means "animation" of any kind, but if we're talking about anime in a western userbase discussion, then it strictly means animation made in Japan, aimed at audience of 10 years or older.

The definition of anime is, according to Cambrdige dictionary is the following:

› Japanese films made using characters and images that are drawn rather than real, or one of these films: Until recently, anime had little more than a cult following outside Japan. an anime that blurs the line between man and machine

The definition in the west doesn't really exist in Japan, from what I know, they just have "animation". But oh well, this is the definition we have in the west regardless of that. So, with this definition in mind the questions become easy.

Does aesthetic style matter when classifying anime (keep in mind the typical anime style versus something like Panty and Stocking)?

Not at all.

Does animation style matter (2D vs 3D) matter when classifying anime?

Not at all.

Original air location (keep in mind Space Dandy came out in America first)?

Not at all.

Is RWBY an anime?

Which definition of 'anime' takes precedence? Western (location of most people on the sub) or Eastern (the country of the term's origin)?

There's only one definition in English, the other is in Japanese. If you're speaking English, then anime = animation from Japan, but if you're speaking Japanese then anime = all animation. Simple as that.

Does Aesthetic style matter when classifying anime?

No not really.

Does animation style (2D vs 3D) matter when classifying anime?

Is RWBY an anime?

Ah yes RWBY. The show that will get entire comment chains nuked just for even glancing over it over on that other site. I, personally, think that RWBY is an anime. I really enjoyed RWBY. I watched it before I got into anime, and didn't say to myself "this is such a great anime!" while I was watching it but I still feel that it falls under that category.

It's artstyle, despite the 3D aspect, is a near exact mirror of anime artstyle. Just because it originated in America doesn't mean it's not anime.

Plus, Newtype has it ranked as the 7th most popular anime of August 2015. I think that gives it credibility as being an anime.

I'm always curious as to why people don't feel RWBY is an anime. It seems the main reasons are:

  • It didn't originate in Japan. To me personally RWBY is no different than a dubbed anime honestly.

  • It's not televised, it's a web series. I don't watch any anime televised, it's all netflix/some other streaming service, what difference does it make?

What definition of 'anime' takes precedence? Western (location of most people on the sub) or Eastern (the country of the term's origin)?

Well that depends on which region you're in. As the majority of us are in the west we should use the western definition of anime. We have a word for the eastern definition: cartoon. It's kind of like 'otaku.' A bunch of people in the west have taken otaku and used it to mean anime nerd/ a fan of Japanese culutre, while in the east 'otaku' has a really negative meaning. It'd make no sense for us to use the eastern definition here and the western definition in Japan.

Does Aesthetic style matter when classifying anime?
No not really.

[RWBY's] artstyle, despite the 3D aspect, is a near exact mirror of anime artstyle. Just because it originated in America doesn't mean it's not anime.

Can you clear that up a bit?

I think that aesthetic style does factor in when classifying anime (in the western definition). It is a varied art form but there are still qualities in the typical style that differentiates it from the typical style of western cartoons. I acknowledge that there are deviations from the definition I am presenting but I think the generalization is hard to ignore. Eyes, hair, how bodies are exaggerated--they all have their own way of being portrayed in both western animation and Japanese animation.

Then we have western productions like the Legend of Korra and there's PSG in Japan. I think that's where the limit of the above defining factor lies. But when I think about it, I refer to Korra as a cartoon, PSG as an anime (just barely), while I see RWBY as a western anime. I do believe aesthetics play into what defines anime but what else is there?

I think another factor would be culture. From things like anime focusing a lot on school settings to displaying different societal norms/social cues to how people use certain forms of transportation. Each form of media tends to reflect the culture it originated from and I guess that, plus other factors like aesthetic, all adds up to "anime".

I guess we can also just consider where the show was produced. What are your thoughts on that?

While I may have exaggerated a bit with "near exact mirror" when mentioning RWBY, there are still far more similarities in the show to that of anime rather than cartoons here in the west. RWBY shares the basic character design elements you mentioned that all anime's seem to possess. I think a bit of that is lost with the 3D style, but I also feel that enough of it remains for it to be mainly anime. (BTW i really like your classification of it as a 'western anime', I feel that's the perfect way to describe it.) For example take Knights of Sidonia, an anime that is largely extremely well received. It uses the 3D artstyle and it has a lot of the same character design (physically that is) as most animes do. RWBY also has these, yet it also has enough variation that it isn't typical anime. These variations include:

  • The crowds in the show. Everyone that's not a major main character or side character is just a silhouette.

  • For me personally, weapon design. Now I love the weapons in RWBY, easily my favorite part of the show. However the transforming weapons in RWBY don't feel like typical anime weapons to me. The closest comparison I can make, and it is a weak one, is to that of the Dominators in Psycho Pass.

I can't comment on environmental design, as that seems to drastically change from anime to anime. Fate/Zero's environments look drastically different from Psycho-Pass which looks drastically different than AoT, etc etc.

I think another major thing we have to look at when classifying something as an anime is tropes and character personality. I may be too inexperienced in anime to draw meaningful conclusions here, but I think RWBY also shares a lot of similarities with typical anime here.

  • Focus on girls. Maybe this is just in loli or something idk. Modoka Magica schoolgirls gotta save the world from evil dark magic, RWBY schoolgirls gotta save the world from dark magic. Yang in RWBY also seems like a typical fan service but still powerful character, like SAO minor

  • That one enthusiastic quirky friend of the MC. The Lisbeth from SAO or the Sayaka from Madoka Magica. RWBY has this in Nora I fell, and to an extent Yang I guess since Nora is on JNPR.

  • The MC that's unsure in their power but is actually secretly really strong! Eren from AoT. RWBY's got Juane.

  • The douchebag ally! The Jean from AoT. That inspector that came in during Psycho-Pass 2 whose name I forgot but everyone hated. You have this in pretty much every member of CRDL in RWBY.

I'm sure there are more tropes that are commonplace that I'm missing but whatever.

TL;DR I think RWBY shares a lot of elements with typical anime, but differers enough that it isn't solely anime. I think @ThisisforPosting's description of "western anime" is a perfect fit, especially considering how we define anime in the west.

I think another major thing we have to look at when classifying something as an anime is tropes and character personality.
